SRC-352:R002.text: 1. P0 — PUBLICATION RECEIPT REUSED AS FOREIGN QUALIFICATION: TICKET: AUT31-001 PRIORITY: P0 SEVERITY: PUBLISHER PROVENANCE BYPASS LOCATOR: tools/producer_backends/saipal_adapter.py ::deliver_finding_to_audit_inbox PREVIOUS REPAIR T-1967 introduced producer-owned qualification records for dict-shaped artifact proofs. Preserve that repair. NEW ROOT CAUSE The alternative string qualification_receipt branch accepts a receipt string when it exists anywhere in: collect_publication_receipts(root) It compares the supplied string to existing receipt_id or operation_id fields. It does not establish that the receipt belongs to the requested finding, immutable artifact, producer generation or qualification. A publication receipt for finding A can therefore authorize publication of unrelated finding B at this adapter boundary. REPRODUCED NEGATIVE CONTROL Disposable project, actual canonical enqueue: 1. Create and legitimately qualify PAL-TRUSTED. 2. Publish PAL-TRUSTED successfully. 3. Preserve its real publication operation ID: saipal-pal-trusted 4. Construct an unrelated PAL-UNRELATED. 5. Give PAL-UNRELATED: state = QUALIFIED qualification_receipt = saipal-pal-trusted new audit_body and corresponding digest 6. Invoke delivery with publication_authorized=True. OBSERVED PAL-TRUSTED: DELIVERED_PUBLICATION PAL-UNRELATED: DELIVERED_PUBLICATION ok = true layer = 2 This reproduction used the real local audit enqueue in a disposable project, not a mocked enqueue callback. It demonstrates a publisher-level qualification bypass. It does not independently prove a bypass of the external campaign grant, broker authorization or installed host boundaries. REPAIR A publication receipt is evidence of a previous destination write, not qualification authority for arbitrary future evidence. Remove the bare-string shortcut, or resolve it through a trusted typed qualification registry with exact identity binding. Require: - producer identity; - trusted producer generation; - original finding identity; - qualification decision identity; - original immutable artifact identity; - immutable artifact digest; - applicable historical protocol; - publication scope; - destination project lineage; - independently verified qualification record. The verified qualification must refer to the SAME finding and SAME immutable artifact being delivered. Do not use a prior published operation ID as a universal token. Do not substitute caller-supplied matching strings for origin proof. Preserve legitimate producer-owned qualification flow. Preserve STAGE_ONLY and independent publication authorization. REQUIRED REGRESSION CONTROLS A01. Genuine receipt belonging to finding A is used for finding B. Expected: refusal, no enqueue. A02. Genuine receipt with another artifact digest. Expected: refusal. A03. Genuine receipt with another project lineage. Expected: refusal. A04. Genuine receipt with another source generation. Expected: refusal unless producer-authenticated revision. A05. Invented string receipt. Expected: refusal. A06. Valid broker-qualified finding with exact matching evidence. Expected: accepted exactly once. A07. Valid producer artifact route. Expected: existing positive behavior preserved. A08. Publication not authorized. Expected: STAGED, no destination write. A09. Concurrent identical delivery. Expected: one canonical operation. A10. Crash after enqueue and before local acknowledgment. Expected: reconcile original receipt. This security repair must be independently verified before unattended forensic publication is enabled.

SRC-352:R003.text: 2. P0 — LEGACY ACK STILL HIDES NEW FINDING REVISIONS: TICKET: AUT31-002 PRIORITY: P0 SEVERITY: SILENT FORENSIC EVIDENCE LOSS LOCATORS: tools/producer_backends/saipal_adapter.py ::_acknowledged_ids ::_legacy_rows_for_corpus ::_committed_publication_ids ::iter_new_qualified_findings PREVIOUS REPAIR T-1969 correctly changed normal committed-publication suppression to compare finding ID and artifact digest. Its positive and negative tests pass. Preserve that implementation. NEW ROOT CAUSE The legacy acknowledgment branch still produces a bare set of finding IDs. _legacy_rows_for_corpus receives source_digest but does not use it to prove that the previous publication belongs to this corpus. It returns legacy IDs whenever the allocator contains any committed record for that finding ID. _acknowledged_ids then adds the ID to the acknowledged set. The page walker checks: if fid in acknowledged: return True before comparing the artifact digest of the current row. Therefore the legacy path bypasses the revision-aware protection. REPRODUCED NEGATIVE CONTROL Disposable project: 1. Qualify and publish PAL-1 with original audit body. 2. Confirm DELIVERED_PUBLICATION. 3. Append a legacy acknowledgment row: finding_ids = [PAL-1] source_digest = null 4. Create new qualified PAL-1 with materially changed audit body. 5. Use a new corpus generation. 6. Walk iter_new_qualified_findings. OBSERVED Old publication: successful. Old artifact digest: 58155025459b... New artifact digest: 7afaf05f29ba... New report yielded: [] Skipped as already delivered: 1 This is a real logical suppression in the current source. The fixture used actual canonical publication for the old finding and isolated report-page input for the new corpus. REPAIR Never reduce a legacy acknowledgment into an unscoped bare-ID suppression authority. A legacy acknowledgment may suppress a row only when its original canonical destination evidence proves the SAME immutable version and applicable generation. The safe fallback for ambiguous legacy evidence is to re-yield the finding and let the idempotent publisher reconcile. Do not silently discard potentially new evidence. Do not blindly republish a conflicting identity either. Preserve conflict detection and explicit revision classification. A possible implementation is to represent acknowledged publication identities as structured records containing: - logical finding ID; - source generation when known; - immutable artifact digest; - producer operation ID; - destination receipt identity. Then compare against the current row's exact verified identity. If a legacy row cannot be scoped, classify it for reconciliation. Do not invent its missing generation retrospectively. Preserve historical bytes and append-only records. REQUIRED CONTROLS B01. Old published PAL-1, legacy ack, changed new PAL-1. Expected: new revision is not silently omitted. B02. Old published PAL-1, unchanged identical replay. Expected: safely suppressed/idempotently reconciled. B03. Legacy ack with no canonical destination receipt. Expected: no unjustified suppression. B04. Legacy ack for another corpus. Expected: no cross-corpus suppression. B05. Scoped ack for exactly the current immutable version. Expected: valid suppression. B06. Multiple revisions under one logical finding. Expected: independent revision identities. B07. Crash between page read and delivery. Expected: finding remains pending. B08. Crash after canonical enqueue. Expected: original publication receipt recovered. B09. Damaged legacy journal. Expected: typed refusal and preserved bytes. B10. Concurrent publication. Expected: no duplicate canonical layers. Never mark this fixed using only the existing T-1969 tests. The new reproduction must be present as a regression test.

SRC-352:R004.text: 3. P1 — DISCOVERY MEMORY AND PARTIAL BATCH DELIVERY: TICKET: AUT31-003 LOCATOR: tools/producer_backends/saipal_adapter.py::discover CURRENT CONDITION The report transport uses a bounded validated spool and pagination. However, discover() still accumulates qualified results: qualified.extend(page.get("findings") or []) The accumulated list grows with the total qualified corpus. A bounded page reader is not a bounded end-to-end consumer. REPAIR Make qualified finding consumption batch-oriented through the actual campaign-owned publication loop. Avoid collecting all qualified findings before processing. Pin each batch to an immutable report generation. Persist exact cursor and pending publication identities. Commit acknowledgment only after verifying canonical delivery. Provide backpressure and bounded resource limits. Support partial success within a page. Support restart without missing or duplicating findings. Do not increase an output cap indefinitely to mask full-report materialization. MEASURE - 100 qualified findings; - 1,000 qualified findings; - 10,000 qualified findings; - backend refusal; - malformed report; - report generation changes mid-walk; - interruption during delivery. Measure peak resident memory and retained state size. Report before/after behavior. Any batch optimization must preserve the P0 repairs above.
